text.insert: Semantic memory represents a codebase expert's current understanding without pretending decompiled identifiers are authoritative. Stable decomp identifiers anchor the record. Human-readable purposes, roles, likely names, game concepts, and relationships are versioned assertions over those anchors.

text.insert: What It Does vs. What It Likely Does

Everything in the knowledge system is inference: the game is not decompiled, so nothing here is ground truth. A claim carries no epistemic category — its confidence alone says how sure we are, its rationale argues from the cited evidence to the value, and the evidence pins exactly what was seen. Structure directly visible in code, assembly, or build output earns high confidence with evidence pointing at the exact spans; an explanation derived from clues states alternatives at a lower confidence; an external statement — wiki, Discord, upstream naming — is cited as evidence and never converted into observed truth. Upstream names that are not raw hex are treated as likely directionally correct, and that belief lives in the confidence, not in a label.

props.title: Invariant — inferred names never become AI source edits

text.insert: An inferred_name assertion is a knowledge alias, not a rename instruction. Worker prompts, edit tools, patch validation, and review lint must treat it as read-only explanatory context. The decomp symbol remains the source anchor and the name is displayed with its confidence, status, and evidence.

A worker may use an alias to reason about a function, field, variable, or parameter and may contribute stronger or competing alias evidence. It must not introduce the alias into identifiers, comments, headers, generated symbols, or source metadata. Human-reviewed upstream naming work remains outside this feature's authority.
